properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 29 at 12:44PM MST until September 29 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 500 PM MST /600 PM MDT/.

* At 1244 PM MST /144 PM MDT/, a river gauge on the Paria River at
Lees Ferry reported a rapid rise of 6 feet from heavy rain over the
Paria River around 10 AM MST. Water levels are falling, but flash
flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Paria Canyon, Paria River Slot Canyon and Lees Ferry.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon!

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 29 at 2:55PM MDT until September 29 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.
Low-water crossings are inundated with water and may not be
passable. Expect many areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 250 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated light-to-moderate rain
over locations that received around 2 inches of rain Monday and
Monday night. Flooding is ongoing in Arroyo Hondo, and expected
to occur in other drainages. Up to 0.3 inches of rain have fallen
today.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.25 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Santa Fe, Eldorado At Santa Fe, La Cienega, Cerrillos Hills State
Park, Los Cerrillos, La Bajada and Agua Fria.
- Around 215 PM, authorities reported homes cutoff due to flooding
in Arroyo Hondo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 29 at 10:45AM EDT until October 1 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Plymouth and Bristol
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles for
an extended period of time.  Beware of the dangers of crossing
flooded roadways. The water may be deeper than you think.
Floodwaters have the ability to damage roadways. Heed the advice of
local officials, and evacuate if asked to do so.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 9.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Tuesday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 6.4 feet Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The South Fork and McBride burn scar in...
South Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 815 PM MDT Tuesday.

* At 211 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Up to 0.7 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the South Fork and McBride
Burn Scars.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork and McBride Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe, San Patricio and Hollywood.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

...FLASH FLOOD WARNING FOR THE IMMINENT FAILURE OF MCLEOD DAM ON THE
MCLEOD ARROYO REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 445 PM MDT THIS AFTERNOON FOR
NORTHWESTERN DONA ANA COUNTY...

At 201 PM MDT, dam operators and county officials reported the
imminent failure of McLeod Dam.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for McLeod Dam. This is a PARTICULARLY
DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding from the imminent failure of
McLeod Dam.

SOURCE...Dam operator.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW!

Rural areas between Garfield and Salem, including portions of
Highways 187 and 390, and along Garfield Drain, Garfield Canal, and
other drainage and irrigation ditches.
properties.instruction:
If you are in low lying areas below the McLeod Dam you should move to
higher ground immediately.
